title: Sweden offshore wind rejections show ‘continuing uncertainty’ – Hexicon
summary: Sweden's rejection of 11 offshore wind projects, including Hexicon's 2.5GW Mareld development, on national security grounds signals regulatory unpredictability that could impair asset valuations and delay returns in Nordic offshore wind portfolios. This geopolitical-driven policy shift creates both near-term headwinds for existing holdings and potential M&A opportunities as distressed sellers seek alternative exit routes.

title: Energy Security Drives Wave of Green Financing
summary: The global sustainable bond market has surged to $810 billion as of August 2026, up 25% YoY, signaling robust institutional capital flows into green infrastructure. This financing momentum creates attractive refinancing opportunities and entry valuations for European infra PE funds targeting energy transition assets.

title: ‘Winter panic’: EU gas stores at their lowest level in 13 years
summary: EU gas storage levels at 13-year lows (63% full vs. 80% historical average) heading into winter, creating significant price volatility risk and potential margin compression for energy infrastructure assets. This supply tightness presents both challenges for leveraged energy transition investments and opportunities for storage, LNG, and supply diversification infrastructure plays.

title: Europe on course for 'record-breaking' wind installations in 2026 despite hurdles
summary: Europe is achieving record wind installations in 2026 despite industry headwinds, signaling strong underlying demand and market resilience for renewable energy assets. This momentum presents attractive deployment opportunities for infrastructure PE funds in both operational wind portfolios and development-stage projects across the region.

title: StepStone Group on private markets’ analytics revolution
summary: Deal-level benchmarking analytics are enabling private markets investors to make more data-driven investment and portfolio decisions, particularly valuable for infrastructure funds seeking competitive returns through better deal sourcing and performance tracking. This technology advancement could reshape how European infrastructure GPs evaluate opportunities and how LPs assess fund performance relative to peers.

title: Global bond sell-off intensifies as US-Iran tensions stoke inflation fears
summary: Rising gilt yields to 5.3% (highest since 2008) driven by US-Iran tensions and inflation fears will increase UK infrastructure financing costs and refinancing pressures. This creates headwinds for leveraged infrastructure deals but may present attractive entry points for long-duration contracted assets with inflation-linked revenues.
pe_angle: Rising rates impact on leverage capacity

title: Defence-Tech Capital Deepens Despite Procurement Bottleneck
summary: European defence procurement is shifting from traditional long-cycle platforms toward rapidly-evolving drone and electronic-warfare technologies, creating fragmented capital requirements and potential consolidation opportunities. This modernization gap presents entry points for PE investors in specialized defence-tech supply chains despite systemic procurement delays.

title: ‘Inept, incompetent, craven’: Scott Bessent struggles to clean up the president’s mess
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faces severe constraints managing a $40tn national debt while executing Trump's Iran sanctions and tariff policies, creating macroeconomic uncertainty that will impact global markets and infrastructure valuations. European infrastructure investors should monitor USD volatility, interest rate trajectories, and potential flight-to-quality effects on European infrastructure assets.

title: Download the September 2026 issue of Private Equity International
summary: This September 2026 issue of PEI examines the expanding secondaries market and profiles emerging fund managers, offering insights into capital deployment trends and fundraising benchmarks. The inclusion of a major sports investing report highlights alternative infrastructure opportunities beyond traditional utilities and transport sectors.

title: Sisk arm Farrans starts work on battery energy storage scheme
summary: Farrans Construction is executing a battery energy storage system (BESS) project in the West Midlands for BW ESS, signaling continued capital deployment in the UK's fast-growing energy storage market as grid operators accelerate decarbonization. This contract win highlights strong underlying demand for storage infrastructure amid renewable penetration growth and represents potential portfolio exposure for PE investors in the critical infrastructure value chain.

title: President Ramaphosa Reaffirms Commitment To Energy Reform
summary: South Africa's president reaffirms commitment to energy reform targeting affordable, reliable, and sustainable electricity supply, signaling continued policy support for infrastructure investment in the sector. This reinforces market confidence for European PE investors considering exposure to sub-Saharan African energy infrastructure through concessions, IPPs, or renewable energy projects.

title: Lithium-ion batteries – the hidden danger on a building site
summary: Lithium-ion battery fire incidents on construction sites represent an emerging operational and liability risk for infrastructure assets, particularly those incorporating energy storage or renewable systems. This trend signals potential need for specialized safety protocols, insurance adjustments, and retrofit opportunities across European construction and infrastructure portfolios.

title: Spitalfields Market gets London’s biggest rooftop solar array
summary: Spitalfields Market's 1.27 GWh annual solar installation represents London's largest rooftop deployment and signals accelerating ESG compliance and capex monetization opportunities for mixed-use urban real estate portfolios. The project exemplifies the renewable energy retrofit market for heritage/commercial assets, where operational savings and subsidy capture can enhance IRRs on stabilized infrastructure plays.

title: Cape Town Seals First Agreements To Buy Power At Below Eskom Rates
summary: Cape Town has secured 200MW of power from independent producers at rates below Eskom's monopoly pricing, signaling a structural shift toward distributed generation and opening procurement opportunities for European renewable developers and operators. This demonstrates accelerating demand for alternative power sources in emerging markets where state utilities face capacity constraints, creating potential acquisition or JV targets for infrastructure funds.

title: What Extreme Weather is Revealing About Regenerative Farming
summary: Extreme weather events are demonstrating the resilience and economic advantages of regenerative farming practices, creating potential infrastructure investment opportunities in agricultural water management, soil remediation, and climate adaptation technologies. European PE investors may find attractive entry points in agtech solutions and land management platforms that support the transition to regenerative systems across fragmented farmland portfolios.

title: Costain doubles apprentice intake to 50
summary: Costain's doubling of apprentice intake to 50 signals confidence in UK infrastructure pipeline demand and addresses critical labor shortages affecting project delivery and margins. This talent investment is strategically important for PE portfolio companies facing execution risks on major infrastructure concessions.

title: ‘UK should clarify reasoning behind Chinese wind restrictions’ – Jonathan Cole
summary: The UK's restrictions on Chinese offshore wind turbine manufacturers lack transparency, creating regulatory uncertainty for European PE investors evaluating UK renewable energy assets and supply chain consolidation opportunities. Policy clarification is critical for assessing long-term returns in offshore wind portfolios and potential M&A targets in the renewable energy sector.

title: Ryanair warns air fares in Europe will jump next year if oil price stays high
summary: Ryanair's warning signals potential airline consolidation risk and fare inflation if elevated oil prices persist, creating headwinds for European aviation and related infrastructure assets. This highlights commodity hedging vulnerabilities across the sector and potential distress opportunities in undercapitalized carriers, while suggesting demand pressures on airport infrastructure investments.

title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest
summary: Barclays faces regulatory complaint over financing a coal-fired power station in Bangladesh, highlighting reputational and ESG risks that European infrastructure investors increasingly face when backing thermal energy projects. The case underscores growing regulatory scrutiny of lender involvement in high-emission assets near sensitive ecosystems, potentially affecting project financing terms and bank participation in emerging market energy infrastructure.

title: AI could cause global economic downturn, Bank of England governor tells G20
summary: Bank of England governor warns that advanced AI poses systemic financial risks and could trigger global economic downturn, potentially affecting credit availability and project financing for infrastructure investments. This regulatory scrutiny may increase compliance costs for infra assets with AI integration while creating opportunities in resilient, regulated utility and transport sectors less exposed to AI disruption.

title: California sues Trump administration over 2GW offshore wind lease buyout
summary: California's lawsuit against the Trump administration over a $150M offshore wind lease buyout signals heightened regulatory risk and political volatility in US renewable energy assets. This creates potential distress opportunities for European PE firms with US exposure while highlighting the importance of political hedging in long-duration infrastructure investments.

title: Beyond Training: Turning Capability Into Opportunities
summary: The article highlights a market gap in construction where women-focused initiatives must evolve beyond training to encompass contract access and business sustainability. This represents an underexploited talent pool and potential ESG value creation opportunity for infrastructure investors backing construction and project delivery platforms across Europe.

title: Maine bucks US trend with go-ahead for 800MW onshore wind farm
summary: Clearway Energy's 800MW Maine wind project represents a significant breakthrough in US onshore wind development, suggesting potential easing of permitting bottlenecks that have constrained US renewables investment. This development could signal improving regulatory conditions for large-scale wind projects, relevant for European PE funds considering US renewable energy exposure or for benchmarking against European wind farm development timelines.

title: Korean GP to court international LPs with sophomore fund
summary: KCGI Private Equity, a Korean GP, is preparing to launch its second fund in 2027, signaling confidence in infrastructure investing and potential capital availability from Asian sources. This development may create competitive pressure for European infra PE funds in fundraising and deal sourcing, particularly if KCGI targets European assets.

title: SAWS Warns Of Very Strong El Niño And Hotter, Drier Spring Conditions
summary: South Africa faces severe drought conditions due to El Niño, creating significant operational risks for water-dependent infrastructure assets and increasing demand for alternative water solutions and energy infrastructure. European PE investors with South African utilities, renewable energy, or water management exposure should reassess climate resilience and consider hedging strategies against extended dry periods.
pe_angle: Climate risk in emerging market utilities

title: Why We Need To Talk About Older People And Climate Change In Africa
summary: African governments' need to develop climate adaptation plans for aging populations creates emerging infrastructure investment opportunities in resilient water, healthcare, and energy systems across the continent. European PE funds can capitalize on ESG-focused infrastructure plays that address demographic vulnerability to climate impacts in underserved African markets.

title: Food Garden Or Swimming Pool? South Africa’s Water Crisis Isn’t Just About A Shortage. It’s About Equality
summary: South Africa faces severe water scarcity driven by infrastructure failure and inequality in resource distribution rather than absolute shortage alone, creating opportunities for infrastructure modernization and management contracts. European PE investors could target water treatment, distribution optimization, and desalination projects addressing both supply constraints and equitable access in emerging markets.

title: Vodacom Challenge Shows South Africans Are Ready To Embrace Responsible E-waste Recycling
summary: Vodacom's e-waste recycling initiative in South Africa demonstrates emerging market demand for circular economy infrastructure and ESG-compliant waste management solutions. This signals growth opportunities for European PE investors in scaling responsible e-waste processing platforms across African markets with strong consumer engagement.

title: NDB And South Africa Sign US $405M Loan Agreements For Infrastructure Projects
summary: The NDB's $405M infrastructure financing in South Africa demonstrates emerging market appetite for development bank capital in sub-Saharan Africa, which could signal opportunities for European PE co-investors in regional infrastructure platforms. However, limited deal specifics suggest this is primarily a policy/geopolitical signal rather than an immediate European PE deployment opportunity.

title: Construction professional helps develop new vocational school for young people
summary: A Turner & Townsend executive is developing an employer-led vocational school to address the construction skills gap, a critical bottleneck for infrastructure project delivery across Europe. This signals growing investment in workforce development infrastructure, which could create ancillary opportunities in training, staffing, and labor-efficient construction models.
